title: St. John's weather map site registration record
description: One record per site, one file per record at registry/sites/<id>.yaml. A site is a preferred location and never an allowlist: nothing here restricts where evidence is served. The directional horizon is hand-registered, because no source publishes horizon and obstruction data at the resolution this deployment needs and because buildings, trees and harbour structures are absent from terrain data. A terrain horizon computed from a digital elevation model is a check on the registration and is recorded beside it; it is never substituted for it. The schema states the shape of a horizon; it cannot state that the list holds exactly 360 / bearing_resolution_deg values, so registry/site_audit.py states that.

id.description: The site id, equal to the file stem. This is what provenance names, so it never changes with the name.

note.description: How the horizon was registered and what it is still waiting for. Optional, because the required keys are the record itself; every record written for this change carries it, so a hand registration never travels without saying it is a hand registration.

datum.description: The vertical datum the metres are stated in. An elevation with no datum is not an elevation, so the key is required and the vocabulary is closed.

horizon.description: The hand-registered directional horizon. elevation_deg holds one horizon elevation angle per bearing, starting at true north and stepping clockwise by bearing_resolution_deg, so a complete horizon holds exactly 360 / bearing_resolution_deg values. A null value is a bearing nobody has registered: it is a gap, stated rather than hidden, and registry/site_audit.py names it.

terrain_check.description: The check of the hand registration against a terrain horizon. dem and terrain_elevation_deg may be null only when the status is not_run; the audit states that rule. A not_run check is a disclosure, not an agreement: the terrain horizon is not assumed to agree.

tolerance_deg.description: How far below the terrain horizon a registered angle may sit before the registration fails.

terrain_elevation_deg.description: The terrain horizon on the same bearing grid as horizon.elevation_deg, or null when the check was not run.
